audience: Design-literate founders, creative directors, architects, collectors and premium-brand teams evaluating whether an immersive web experience can create genuine spatial memory rather than decorative motion.
objective: Create a flagship Forge experience that proves a browser can feel like entering a designed place: approach a monumental observatory, cross a physical threshold, descend into an underground light gallery, inspect the instrument, manipulate light, and return to the landscape with a memorable artifact.
primaryAction: Explore the observatory and save a field study
brandTruth: HELIOT is about revealing the unseen by turning light itself into architecture, material and interaction.
differentiators: One continuous real-time world connects exterior landscape, threshold, passage, gallery, exhibit and return flight
The visitor physically crosses the gateway instead of watching a prerecorded flythrough or zooming a still image
The aperture control changes real geometry, GPU ray width, semantic readout and exported field-study artifacts
The signature sequence is spatial: landscape to architecture to underground light, then reconstruction on reverse scroll
The visual language is mineral, architectural and restrained rather than generic sci-fi WebGL
constraints: Do not turn the gateway into a generic product orbit
Do not add neon, floating UI debris, gratuitous particles or unrelated wow effects
Preserve one persistent spatial world and reversible authored camera continuity
Mobile and reduced-motion modes must preserve meaning, controls and chapter access
Use the current Forge runtime, Director, spatial safety and performance systems instead of reviving stale branch architecture
All assets remain local and original; the project must not depend on remote HDRs, fonts, AI services or third-party media
